title: Weekly community
hook: a gathering: a congregation, a group, a meal
tomorrow: what did Jesus tell a crowd of worriers to go and look at?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: one a week, served first in the same row, then serving. The langar is a kitchen, and also a people. Today, the people.

People who leave a church, a team or a hometown sometimes say the hardest part wasn't the beliefs. It was Sunday afternoon, with no one to see. The Buddha's attendant Ananda once came to him with a thought he'd been turning over. Lord, he said, it seems to me that good friendship, good companionship, is half of the holy life. It sounds generous. Half! The Buddha's answer was not the one he expected.
screen: `SUNDAY, WITH NO ONE TO SEE.` → `ANANDA HAS A THOUGHT.` → `FRIENDSHIP IS HALF THE PATH?` → `NOT THE ANSWER HE EXPECTED.`

segments.voice: Not so, Ananda, the Buddha said. Don't say that. Good friendship is the whole of the holy life. Someone with good friends, he went on, can be expected to walk the path. Then he pointed to himself. People bound to birth, aging and death are set free, he said, by relying on me as a good friend. The word is kalyana-mitta, the good friend, the admirable friend. This is why community sits at the center of Buddhist practice, not at its edge. Buddhists take refuge in three things, the Three Refuges: the Buddha, the Dhamma, his teaching, and the Sangha, the community that practices it. The sangha isn't a bonus for people who like groups. It is one third of what Buddhists rely on. Monks and nuns live it every day; lay Buddhists meet at a temple or a meditation group, share food, chant together. Ananda was the Buddha's own attendant, and even he thought friends were a helpful half. The Buddha said they are the whole road: with good friends, a person can be expected to walk it. Weekly community is that teaching made regular: one gathering, the same people, again and again, until they're yours.
screen: `NOT SO, ANANDA: THE WHOLE.` · `KALYANA-MITTA: THE GOOD FRIEND.` · `THE THREE REFUGES.` · `THE SANGHA: A THIRD OF THE REFUGE.` · then, large: `MY PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Picture five chairs around you. In each, seat one person you see often enough to call your own. If a chair stays empty, name one weekly gathering where you might find them, a congregation, a group, a class, a shared meal, and the day it meets.
Weekly community: one gathering you return to every week, the same people, the good friends the Buddha called the whole of the path.
Keep this one: my people, not half the path but the whole of it. Talk soon.
